title: Resolve every wagon artifact URN to a registered contract

facts.note: Wagon artifact files and contract registry files can be identified by path/kind. The constraint is state-based: it applies to every wagon artifact URN, whether or not the file changes in the current edit.

values: orphaned URN (wagon artifact URN with no matching contract in the registry)
facts.note: Needs a resolver that matches each wagon artifact URN (e.g. contract:<domain>:<name>) to registry contract ids (e.g. <domain>:<name>:v*). Source implementation.type is none, so no existing resolver is established. This finding is the firing condition; every firing case requires it.
Only orders remediation when a migration is in progress; phase alone never makes the rule fire, and it does not limit when the constraint applies.

fires: Any wagon artifact URN, new or already existing and unchanged, has no matching contract in the registry (e.g. contract:ux:phantom with no ux:phantom:v* id).
A plan, wagon or registry is inspected or validated (inside or outside a migration) and at least one unresolved wagon artifact URN exists.
A registry contract is removed or renamed and no remaining registry contract matches a wagon artifact URN that referenced it.
A migration phase2 validation finds at least one wagon artifact URN that does not resolve to a registry contract.
doesNotFire: Every wagon artifact URN resolves to an existing registry contract at some version (e.g. contract:ux:foundations -> ux:foundations:v1), including when a migration phase2 validation runs and reports zero unresolved URNs.
A registry contract is removed or renamed but every wagon artifact URN still resolves to a remaining matching contract (e.g. another version).

given: A wagon declares artifact URNs (e.g. contract:<domain>:<name>), whether new or existing, and a contract registry exists.
when: You check, validate, plan or change wagons, their artifacts or the contract registry.
then: Ensure every wagon artifact URN resolves to a matching contract in the registry (e.g. contract:<domain>:<name> -> <domain>:<name>:v*); any unresolved URN is an orphan and a violation.
prefer: Validate that all wagon URNs resolve to registry contracts first (migration phase2), then generate the missing contracts for any orphaned URNs (migration phase3).
Treat orphan detection output as a work list of contracts to create, so each artifact gets a defined schema, version and API.
Check every wagon artifact URN, not only contract:<domain>:<name> ones; if you cannot establish how a URN form maps to a registry id, report it as unresolved rather than skipping it.
avoid: Leaving any wagon artifact URN that names no contract in the registry (e.g. contract:ux:phantom with no ux:phantom:v* id), including pre-existing ones.
Removing or renaming a registry contract when it leaves a wagon URN with no remaining matching contract.
why: URNs are the bidirectional link between wagon artifacts and contracts; a URN that resolves to no contract breaks that link and leaves the artifact's schema, version and API undefined.
evidence: Every wagon artifact URN maps to a registry contract (for contract:<domain>:<name> URNs, an id <domain>:<name> at some version).
Phase2 validation reports zero unresolved URNs; any orphans found were remediated by generating contracts (phase3).
verifier_detail: Resolution example: URN contract:<domain>:<name> matches registry id <domain>:<name>:v<N> for any version N. Positive: contract:ux:foundations resolves to id ux:foundations:v1 (linked, not orphan). Negative: contract:ux:phantom with no contract id ux:phantom:v* in registry (orphan = violation). These are examples; check all wagon artifact URNs, not only those in this form. The source defines no mapping for other URN forms; a URN whose resolution cannot be established is reported as unresolved, not skipped.

Each wagon URN without a matching contract is one violation (orphan_violation), regardless of whether it was changed in the current edit. Term ids: orphan_violation ('Orphaned URN definition'), orphan_remediation ('Resolving orphaned URNs').
Remediation phases: phase2 = validate all URNs resolve to contracts; phase3 = generate missing contracts for orphaned URNs. A phase2 run with zero unresolved URNs is compliant and is not a firing.

additions.justification: Direct consequence of the source obligation (URN must resolve) viewed from the registry side; not a new obligation.
